attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

input.command: cat apps/web/docker-compose.yml && echo "---ENV EXAMPLE---" && cat apps/web/.env.example
input.description: Inspect existing docker-compose and env example

content.content:
# This is meant for local development only. Do not use this in production.
version: "3.8"

services:
  ps-mysql:
    image: mysql:8.0
    restart: always
    environment:
      MYSQL_DATABASE: planetscale
      MYSQL_ROOT_HOST: "%"
      MYSQL_ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD: "yes"
    command:
      [
        "--max_connections=1000",
        "--default-authentication-plugin=mysql_native_password",
      ]
    ports:
      - 3306:3306
    volumes:
      - ps-mysql:/var/lib/mysql

  planetscale-proxy:
    image: ghcr.io/mattrobenolt/ps-http-sim:latest
    command:
      [
        "-mysql-no-pass",
        "-listen-port=3900",
        "-mysql-dbname=planetscale",
        "-mysql-addr=ps-mysql",
      ]
    depends_on:
      - ps-mysql
    ports:
      - 3900:3900
    links:
      - ps-mysql

  mailhog:
    image: "mailhog/mailhog:latest"
    ports:
      - "1025:1025"
      - "8025:8025"

volumes:
  ps-mysql:
---ENV EXAMPLE---
###############################
###### REQUIRED ENV VARS ######
###############################

NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=Dub
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_DOMAIN=dub.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_SHORT_DOMAIN=dub.sh

# Generate a random secret here: https://generate-secret.vercel.app/32
NEXTAUTH_SECRET=
NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:8888 # (only needed for localhost)

# MySQL Database via Planetscale
# Get your MySQL Database URL here: https://planetscale.com/docs/tutorials/connect-nodejs-app
DATABASE_URL="mysql://root:@localhost:3306/planetscale"
# Set local development documentation for connecting to a local database: https://dub.co/docs/local-development#step-4-set-up-planetscale-mysql-database
PLANETSCALE_DATABASE_URL="http://root:unused@localhost:3900/planetscale"

# Upstash Redis – required for Redis caching
# Get your Redis REST URL and Token here: https://upstash.com/docs/redis/overall/getstarted
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL=
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN=

# Upstash QStash – required for queues and background jobs
# Get your QStash Token here: https://upstash.com/docs/qstash/overall/getstarted
QSTASH_TOKEN=
QSTASH_CURRENT_SIGNING_KEY=
QSTASH_NEXT_SIGNING_KEY=

# Tinybird – required for analytics 
# Get your Tinybird Auth Token here: https://www.tinybird.co/docs/concepts/auth-tokens.html
TINYBIRD_API_KEY=
# Varies based on your Tinybird region: https://www.tinybird.co/docs/api-reference/api-reference.html#regions-and-endpoints
TINYBIRD_API_URL=https://api.tinybird.co

# Vercel's Domains API – required for adding and removing domains
# Learn how to set this up: https://vercel.com/templates/next.js/domains-api
PROJECT_ID_VERCEL=
TEAM_ID_VERCEL=
AUTH_BEARER_TOKEN=

# Required for email login
# Get your Resend API Key here: https://resend.com/api-keys
RESEND_API_KEY=
# Resend webhook secret for webhook verification
RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET=

# SMTP configuration (Recommended for local development)
SMTP_HOST=localhost
SMTP_PORT=1025
SMTP_USER=smtpUser
SMTP_PASSWORD=smtpPassword

# Email unsubscribe token secret (optional, falls back to NEXTAUTH_SECRET)
UNSUBSCRIBE_TOKEN_SECRET=

###############################
###### OPTIONAL ENV VARS ######
###############################

# Stripe – used for subscriptions
# If you don't need this, you can also remove the `lib/stripe` folder and all instances of `stripe` from the codebase
NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=
STRIPE_CONNECT_WEBHOOK_SECRET=
STRIPE_CONNECT_V2_WEBHOOK_SECRET=

# Stripe Integration
STRIPE_APP_WEBHOOK_SECRET=
STRIPE_APP_SECRET_KEY=
STRIPE_APP_SECRET_KEY_TEST=
STRIPE_APP_SECRET_KEY_SANDBOX=

# Shopify App webhook events
SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET=

# Used for Google Login
# Learn how to set this up here: https://next-auth.js.org/providers/google
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=

# Used for GitHub Login
# Learn how to set this up here: https://next-auth.js.org/providers/github
GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=
GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=

# Edge Config – used for admin features like banning users, rate limiting etc.
# Create one here: https://vercel.com/docs/storage/edge-config
# Alternatively, if you don't need this, you can also remove `lib/edge-config.ts`
# and all instances of `EDGE_CONFIG` and `EDGE_CONFIG_ID` from the codebase
EDGE_CONFIG=
EDGE_CONFIG_ID=

# Bitly Importer: https://dub.co/blog/migration-assistants
# Apply for an API key here: https://dev.bitly.com/
BITLY_CLIENT_ID=
BITLY_CLIENT_SECRET=

# Used for Custom Link Previews feature
# Apply for an API key here: https://unsplash.com/developers
UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY=

# Use for storing image assets
STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY_ID=
STORAGE_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=
STORAGE_ENDPOINT=
STORAGE_BASE_URL=
STORAGE_PUBLIC_BUCKET=
STORAGE_PRIVATE_BUCKET=

# Used for internal monitoring & paging
# You can remove this by removing `DUB_SLACK_HOOK_CRON` and `DUB_SLACK_HOOK_LINKS` from the codebase
DUB_SLACK_HOOK_CRON=
DUB_SLACK_HOOK_LINKS=

# Used for background jobs
# Get your ngrok URL here: https://ngrok.com/
NEXT_PUBLIC_NGROK_URL=

# For AI features
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=

# Axiom – used for logging and monitoring
# Get your Axiom token here: https://axiom.co/docs/rest-api/authentication
AXIOM_TOKEN=
AXIOM_DATASET=

# Plain – used for customer support integration
# Get your Plain API key here: https://www.plain.com/docs/api
PLAIN_API_KEY=
PLAIN_WEBHOOK_SECRET=

######################################
###### DUB.CO INTERNAL USE ONLY ######
######################################

# For the official Dub app
NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_DUB=

# For cron jobs
CRON_SECRET=

# For support docs embedding sync
EMBEDDING_SYNC_SECRET=
UPSTASH_VECTOR_REST_URL=
UPSTASH_VECTOR_REST_TOKEN=

# Slack integration
SLACK_CLIENT_ID=
SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET=
SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET=

# Dynadot API key for domain registration
DYNADOT_API_KEY=
DYNADOT_BASE_URL=
DYNADOT_COUPON=

# Partner Platforms Verification
TWITTER_CLIENT_ID=
TWITTER_CLIENT_SECRET=
TIKTOK_CLIENT_ID=
TIKTOK_CLIENT_SECRET=
YOUTUBE_API_KEY=

# Scrape Creators
SCRAPECREATORS_API_KEY=

# Paypal
PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID=
PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET=
PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID=

# Program lander generation
FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=

# for generating planetscale backups (https://planetscale.com/docs/api/service-tokens)
PLANETSCALE_SERVICE_TOKEN=

# Hubspot
HUBSPOT_CLIENT_ID=
HUBSPOT_CLIENT_SECRET=

# E2E Playwright Tests
PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL=http://partners.localhost:8888
E2E_PARTNER_EMAIL=
E2E_PARTNER_PASSWORD=

# Veriff (Identity Verification)
VERIFF_API_KEY=
VERIFF_SHARED_SECRET=

Our platform powers 100M+ clicks and 2M+ links monthly, and is used by world-class marketing teams from companies like Twilio, Buffer, Framer, Perplexity, Vercel, Laravel, and [more](https://dub.co/customers). ## Tech Stack - [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) – framework - [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) – language - [Tailwind](https://tailwindcss.com/) – CSS - [Prisma](https://www.prisma.io/) – ORM - [Upstash](https://upstash.com/) – redis - [Tinybird](https://tinybird.com/) – analytics - [PlanetScale](https://planetscale.com/) – database - [NextAuth.js](https://next-auth.js.org/) – auth - [BoxyHQ](https://boxyhq.com/enterprise-sso) – SSO/SAML - [Turborepo](https://turbo.build/repo) – monorepo - [Stripe](https://stripe.com/) – payments - [Resend](https://resend.com/) – emails - [Vercel](https://vercel.com/) – deployments ## Self-Hosting You can self-host Dub for greater control over your data and design. [Read this guide](https://dub.co/docs/self-hosting/guide) to learn more. ## Contributing We love our contributors! Here's how you can contribute: - [Open an issue](https://github.com/dubinc/dub/issues) if you believe you've encountered a bug. - Follow the [local development guide](https://dub.co/docs/local-development) to get your local dev environment set up. - Make a [pull request](https://github.com/dubinc/dub/pull) to add new features/make quality-of-life improvements/fix bugs. ### Recommended Versions | Package | Version | | ------- | -------- | | node | v23.11.0 | | pnpm | 9.15.9 | ### Common Local Development Issues - `The table does not exist in the current database.` - Run `pnpm prisma:push` push the state of the Prisma schema file to the database without using migrations files. - The project is not building correctly locally - verify your versions of `node` and `pnpm` match the recommended versions above. Delete all `node_modules`, `.next`, and `.turbo` directories in the `apps` and `packages` directory. I'm setting up the Dub repo (https://github.com/dubinc/dub) for an Alloy dev sandbox. The repo is at /workspace. I need to identify the bare minimum services and config needed to get the Next.js frontend (apps/web) booting, even if some features are unavailable.

Please report on:
1. What `localhost` (no port, no subdomain) routes to in middleware — is the home page reachable, or does it always redirect to /login? Confirm /login renders without needing a logged-in session.
2. Where the Upstash Redis REST API client is initialized (look in apps/web/lib/upstash, apps/web/lib/redis, packages/utils). Does the app crash at startup if UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL is missing, or does it gracefully degrade? Are there alternatives like serverless-redis-http or hiett/serverless-redis-http that could be used as a Docker container to provide the Upstash REST API on top of plain Redis?
3. Where Tinybird is initialized — does it crash without TINYBIRD_API_KEY?
4. Where QStash, Stripe, Edge Config, Resend are initialized — do they crash without keys?
5. The NextAuth config — does it require a database connection at boot?
6. Check if there's any existing local dev guide at apps/web/README.md or in docs/. Look at how apps/web/docker-compose.yml is intended to be used with the .env.example.
7. Whether the dev server's port 8888 can be overridden via env var, or only via the `--port` flag in apps/web/package.json's "dev" script.

Be concrete with file paths and line numbers. Focus on what's needed to boot, not feature completeness. Under 500 words.

content.text:
Perfect. Now let me create a comprehensive report with all the findings.

## Report: Dub Next.js Frontend Minimum Boot Requirements

### 1. **Localhost Routing & Home Page Access**
- **Middleware** (`/workspace/apps/web/middleware.ts:43-44`): Requests to `APP_HOSTNAMES` are routed to `AppMiddleware`.
- **AppMiddleware** (`/workspace/apps/web/lib/middleware/app.ts:23-42`): Unauthenticated users requesting `/` are redirected to `/login?next=/`. 
- **Login page** (`/workspace/apps/web/app/app.dub.co/(auth)/login/page.tsx:12-42`): Renders without authentication. No database queries required for initial page load.
- **Verdict**: The home page always redirects to `/login`, but `/login` renders successfully without a logged-in session.

### 2. **Upstash Redis REST API**
- **Initialization** (`/workspace/apps/web/lib/upstash/redis.ts:1-30`):
  - `Redis` clients are instantiated with empty string defaults (lines 5-6): `process.env.UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL || ""` and token likewise.
  - Three instances created: `redis`, `redisGlobal`, and `redisGlobalWithTimeout`.
  - **No crash at startup** — the clients accept empty credentials and defer connection until first use.
- **Alternative**: No built-in fallback; however, `serverless-redis-http` or `hiett/serverless-redis-http` could wrap plain Redis with Upstash-compatible REST API.
- **Verdict**: App boots gracefully without Redis keys; features requiring caching will fail at runtime.

### 3. **Tinybird**
- **Initialization** (`/workspace/apps/web/lib/tinybird/client.ts:1-6`):
  - `new Tinybird({ token: process.env.TINYBIRD_API_KEY as string, baseUrl: process.env.TINYBIRD_API_URL as string })`
  - Uses `as string` assertion without null check.
- **Verdict**: **Will crash at startup if `TINYBIRD_API_KEY` is missing**, as the type assertion ignores undefined values and the client fails on first use. The `.env.example` comments (line 30) mark it as "required for analytics."

### 4. **QStash, Stripe, Edge Config, Resend**
- **QStash** (`/workspace/apps/web/lib/cron/index.ts:1-5`): `new Client({ token: process.env.QSTASH_TOKEN || "" })` — **graceful degradation**, boots without token.
- **Stripe** (`/workspace/apps/web/lib/stripe/index.ts:4-5`): `new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY)` — **crashes at startup if `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is missing**.
- **Edge Config** (`/workspace/apps/web/lib/edge-config/is-blacklisted-email.ts:4`): Checked at runtime with try-catch; guarded by `if (!process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_DUB || !process.env.EDGE_CONFIG)` — **no crash**.
- **Resend** (`/workspace/packages/email/src/resend/client.ts:3-5`): `process.env.RESEND_API_KEY ? new Resend(...) : null` — **graceful degradation**, boots without key.
- **Verdict**: Only Stripe crashes; QStash and Resend gracefully degrade; Edge Config is optional.

### 5. **NextAuth Configuration**
- **Config** (`/workspace/apps/web/lib/auth/options.ts:71-621`):
  - Uses `PrismaAdapter` (line 351), which requires a database connection.
  - Calls to `prisma.user.findUnique()`, `prisma.user.create()`, etc. are deferred to runtime (callbacks, not at initialization).
  - `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` is not validated at startup (line 10).
- **Verdict**: **Requires database at runtime** (not boot-time), triggered by first auth attempt. Boot succeeds without database; auth fails at runtime.

### 6. **Local Development Documentation**
- **README** (`/workspace/README.md:62`): References "Follow the [local development guide](https://dub.co/docs/local-development)" — external URL, not in repo.
- **Docker Compose** (`/workspace/apps/web/docker-compose.yml`): Provides MySQL (port 3306), PlanetScale proxy (port 3900), and MailHog (port 1025). **No Redis, no Tinybird, no QStash services**. Aligns with `.env.example` noting these as external.
- **Verdict**: Guide is external. Docker Compose covers database and SMTP only.

### 7. **Dev Server Port Override**
- **Dev Script** (`/workspace/apps/web/package.json:6`): 
  ```
  "dev": "concurrently ... \"pnpm prisma:generate && next dev --turbopack --port 8888\" ..."
  ```
  Port is **hardcoded as 8888**, passed directly to the `next dev` command.
- **Verdict**: Cannot be overridden via env var; requires modifying `package.json` or passing `--port` flag directly (not exposed in script).

---

### **Minimum Boot Requirements Summary**

| Service | Required | Crashes | Gracefully Degrades |
|---------|----------|---------|-------------------|
| MySQL Database | No (runtime only) | — | Yes |
| Upstash Redis | No | No | Yes |
| Tinybird | **Yes** | **Yes** | No |
| QStash | No | No | Yes |
| Stripe | **Yes** | **Yes** | No |
| Resend | No | No | Yes |
| Edge Config | No | No | Yes |

**To boot the frontend minimally:**
1. Provide `TINYBIRD_API_KEY` and `TINYBIRD_API_URL`, or stub the Tinybird client.
2. Provide `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, or modify `/workspace/apps/web/lib/stripe/index.ts` to use optional initialization.
3. Database connection only needed for login flow (runtime, not boot).

input.content:
# Alloy dev-env compose file for the Dub monorepo.
#
# Boots the apps/web Next.js dev server on http://localhost:8080 along with the
# minimum infra needed to make a meaningful page render: a MySQL database, the
# PlanetScale HTTP proxy that the app speaks to in dev, plain Redis with the
# hiett/serverless-redis-http shim that emulates Upstash's REST API, and a
# MailHog SMTP catcher so email sends don't crash.
#
# All services use network_mode: host so the Next.js app and the supporting
# services can reach each other via 127.0.0.1 with no extra DNS plumbing.

services:
  mysql:
    image: mysql:8.0
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      MYSQL_DATABASE: planetscale
      MYSQL_ROOT_HOST: "%"
      MYSQL_ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD: "yes"
    command:
      - "--max_connections=1000"
      - "--default-authentication-plugin=mysql_native_password"
      - "--bind-address=127.0.0.1"
    volumes:
      - mysql-data:/var/lib/mysql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "mysqladmin", "ping", "-h", "127.0.0.1", "-uroot"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

  planetscale-proxy:
    image: ghcr.io/mattrobenolt/ps-http-sim:latest
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    command:
      - "-mysql-no-pass"
      - "-listen-addr=127.0.0.1"
      - "-listen-port=3900"
      - "-mysql-dbname=planetscale"
      - "-mysql-addr=127.0.0.1"
      - "-mysql-port=3306"
    depends_on:
      mysql:
        condition: service_healthy

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["redis-server", "--bind", "127.0.0.1", "--port", "6379"]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "-h", "127.0.0.1", "ping"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  # Upstash Redis REST API emulator on top of plain Redis.
  # Listens on 127.0.0.1:8079 and forwards to the redis service above.
  serverless-redis-http:
    image: hiett/serverless-redis-http:latest
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      SRH_MODE: env
      SRH_TOKEN: dub-local-token
      SRH_CONNECTION_STRING: "redis://127.0.0.1:6379"
      SRH_PORT: "8079"
    depends_on:
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

  mailhog:
    image: mailhog/mailhog:latest
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    # MailHog binds to all interfaces by default; SMTP on 1025, UI on 8025.

  # One-shot job: install workspace dependencies and push the Prisma schema to
  # MySQL so the app has a usable schema when first hit.
  web-bootstrap:
    image: node:22-bookworm
    network_mode: host
    working_dir: /workspace
    restart: "no"
    env_file:
      - .alloy/web.env
    volumes:
      - .:/workspace
      - pnpm-store:/root/.local/share/pnpm/store
    depends_on:
      mysql:
        condition: service_healthy
      planetscale-proxy:
        condition: service_started
    command:
      - "bash"
      - "-lc"
      - |
        set -e
        corepack enable
        corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.9 --activate
        pnpm install --frozen-lockfile=false
        pnpm --filter=@dub/prisma generate
        # Push schema; tolerate transient failures so the dev server can still
        # boot and render the login page even if the DB isn't ready yet.
        pnpm --filter=@dub/prisma push --accept-data-loss --skip-generate || true
        echo "web-bootstrap: done"

  web:
    image: node:22-bookworm
    network_mode: host
    working_dir: /workspace/apps/web
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file:
      - .alloy/web.env
    volumes:
      - .:/workspace
      - pnpm-store:/root/.local/share/pnpm/store
    depends_on:
      web-bootstrap:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    command:
      - "bash"
      - "-lc"
      - |
        set -e
        corepack enable
        corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.9 --activate
        # Ensure the prisma client exists for the dev server.
        pnpm --filter=@dub/prisma generate
        # Boot Next.js on port 8080 (Alloy convention). We bypass the package
        # script's hardcoded --port 8888 and skip Prisma Studio.
        exec pnpm exec next dev --turbopack --port 8080 --hostname 0.0.0.0

volumes:
  mysql-data:
  pnpm-store:

content.content:
name: workspace
services:
  mailhog:
    image: mailhog/mailhog:latest
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
  mysql:
    command:
      - --max_connections=1000
      - --default-authentication-plugin=mysql_native_password
      - --bind-address=127.0.0.1
    environment:
      MYSQL_ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD: "yes"
      MYSQL_DATABASE: planetscale
      MYSQL_ROOT_HOST: '%'
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - mysqladmin
        - ping
        - -h
        - 127.0.0.1
        - -uroot
      timeout: 5s
      interval: 5s
      retries: 30
    image: mysql:8.0
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - type: volume
        source: mysql-data
        target: /var/lib/mysql
        volume: {}
  planetscale-proxy:
    command:
      - -mysql-no-pass
      - -listen-addr=127.0.0.1
      - -listen-port=3900
      - -mysql-dbname=planetscale
      - -mysql-addr=127.0.0.1
      - -mysql-port=3306
    depends_on:
      mysql:
        condition: service_healthy
        required: true
    image: ghcr.io/mattrobenolt/ps-http-sim:latest
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
  redis:
    command:
      - redis-server
      - --bind
      - 127.0.0.1
      - --port
      - "6379"
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - redis-cli

# Alloy dev-env compose file for the Dub monorepo.
#
# Boots the apps/web Next.js dev server on http://localhost:8080 along with the
# minimum infra needed to make a meaningful page render: a MySQL database, the
# PlanetScale HTTP proxy that the app speaks to in dev, plain Redis with the
# hiett/serverless-redis-http shim that emulates Upstash's REST API, and a
# MailHog SMTP catcher so email sends don't crash.
#
# All services use network_mode: host so the Next.js app and the supporting
# services can reach each other via 127.0.0.1 with no extra DNS plumbing.

services:
  mysql:
    image: mysql:8.0
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      MYSQL_DATABASE: planetscale
      MYSQL_ROOT_HOST: "%"
      MYSQL_ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD: "yes"
    command:
      - "--max_connections=1000"
      - "--default-authentication-plugin=mysql_native_password"
      - "--bind-address=127.0.0.1"
    volumes:
      - mysql-data:/var/lib/mysql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "mysqladmin", "ping", "-h", "127.0.0.1", "-uroot"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

  planetscale-proxy:
    image: ghcr.io/mattrobenolt/ps-http-sim:latest
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    command:
      - "-mysql-no-pass"
      - "-listen-addr=127.0.0.1"
      - "-listen-port=3900"
      - "-mysql-dbname=planetscale"
      - "-mysql-addr=127.0.0.1"
      - "-mysql-port=3306"
    depends_on:
      mysql:
        condition: service_healthy

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["redis-server", "--bind", "127.0.0.1", "--port", "6379"]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "-h", "127.0.0.1", "ping"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  # Upstash Redis REST API emulator on top of plain Redis.
  # Listens on 127.0.0.1:8079 and forwards to the redis service above.
  serverless-redis-http:
    image: hiett/serverless-redis-http:latest
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      SRH_MODE: env
      SRH_TOKEN: dub-local-token
      SRH_CONNECTION_STRING: "redis://127.0.0.1:6379"
      SRH_PORT: "8079"
    depends_on:
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

  mailhog:
    image: mailhog/mailhog:latest
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    # MailHog binds to all interfaces by default; SMTP on 1025, UI on 8025.

  # One-shot job: install workspace dependencies and push the Prisma schema to
  # MySQL so the app has a usable schema when first hit.
  web-bootstrap:
    image: node:22-bookworm
    network_mode: host
    working_dir: /workspace
    restart: "no"
    env_file:
      - .alloy/web.env
    volumes:
      - .:/workspace
      - pnpm-store:/root/.local/share/pnpm/store
    depends_on:
      mysql:
        condition: service_healthy
      planetscale-proxy:
        condition: service_started
    command:
      - "bash"
      - "-lc"
      - |
        set -e
        corepack enable
        corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.9 --activate

I see the issue — `/login` is returning a "Link not found" error because the middleware is incorrectly classifying `localhost:8080` as a link domain instead of recognizing it as the app hostname. The problem is in how the APP_HOSTNAMES set is configured in the constants file, which only includes the production and preview subdomains but doesn't account for the local development environment.

Looking at the hardcoded values, `localhost:8888` is explicitly listed, but our app is running on port 8080, so when the middleware checks the `req.headers.host` value, it won't find a match. Even though bare "localhost" is in the set, the parsing function might be including the port number in the domain extraction, which would cause the lookup to fail.

I need to trace through how the parse function handles the host header to understand whether it strips the port or keeps it intact.

content.thinking: The domain from the request header is `localhost:8080`, but the allowed hostnames only include `localhost:8888` and `localhost` without a port, so there's a mismatch. I can either update the constants file to use port 8080 or switch the dev server to run on 8888 instead. I'm realizing the cleanest solution is to use a reverse proxy like Caddy that listens on 8080, forwards requests to the dev server on 8888, and rewrites the Host header to match what the middleware expects—this way the application sees the correct hostname without modifying the source code.

content.text: The middleware checks the Host header against a hardcoded `localhost:8888` whitelist, treating any other port as a link-shortener domain. Cleanest fix: run Next on 8888 internally and front it with a tiny Caddy reverse proxy on 8080 that rewrites the Host header.

web:
    image: node:22-bookworm
    network_mode: host
    working_dir: /workspace/apps/web
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file:
      - .alloy/web.env
    volumes:
      - .:/workspace
      - pnpm-store:/root/.local/share/pnpm/store
    depends_on:
      web-bootstrap:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    command:
      - "bash"
      - "-lc"
      - |
        set -e
        corepack enable
        corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.9 --activate
        # Ensure the prisma client exists for the dev server.
        pnpm --filter=@dub/prisma generate
        # Boot Next.js on the upstream port 8888 — that hostname is hardcoded
        # into APP_HOSTNAMES inside packages/utils, so the app's middleware
        # only treats requests as the dashboard if the Host header is
        # localhost:8888. The "alloy-proxy" service below exposes the public
        # 8080 port and rewrites the Host header on the way through.
        exec pnpm exec next dev --turbopack --port 8888 --hostname 127.0.0.1

  # Public-facing reverse proxy: localhost:8080 -> localhost:8888 with the
  # Host header rewritten to "localhost:8888" so the Next.js middleware
  # routes the request to the app dashboard instead of treating the public
  # port as an unknown short-link domain.
  alloy-proxy:
    image: caddy:2-alpine
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - web
    command:
      - "caddy"
      - "reverse-proxy"
      - "--from"
      - ":8080"
      - "--to"
      - "127.0.0.1:8888"
      - "--change-host-header"

# Alloy dev-env compose file for the Dub monorepo.
#
# Boots the apps/web Next.js dev server on http://localhost:8080 along with the
# minimum infra needed to make a meaningful page render: a MySQL database, the
# PlanetScale HTTP proxy that the app speaks to in dev, plain Redis with the
# hiett/serverless-redis-http shim that emulates Upstash's REST API, and a
# MailHog SMTP catcher so email sends don't crash.
#
# All services use network_mode: host so the Next.js app and the supporting
# services can reach each other via 127.0.0.1 with no extra DNS plumbing.

services:
  mysql:
    image: mysql:8.0
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      MYSQL_DATABASE: planetscale
      MYSQL_ROOT_HOST: "%"
      MYSQL_ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD: "yes"
    command:
      - "--max_connections=1000"
      - "--default-authentication-plugin=mysql_native_password"
      - "--bind-address=127.0.0.1"
    volumes:
      - mysql-data:/var/lib/mysql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "mysqladmin", "ping", "-h", "127.0.0.1", "-uroot"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

  planetscale-proxy:
    image: ghcr.io/mattrobenolt/ps-http-sim:latest
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    command:
      - "-mysql-no-pass"
      - "-listen-addr=127.0.0.1"
      - "-listen-port=3900"
      - "-mysql-dbname=planetscale"
      - "-mysql-addr=127.0.0.1"
      - "-mysql-port=3306"
    depends_on:

# minimum infra needed to make a meaningful page render: a MySQL database, the

# services can reach each other via 127.0.0.1 with no extra DNS plumbing.

  mysql:
    image: mysql:8.0
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      MYSQL_DATABASE: planetscale
      MYSQL_ROOT_HOST: "%"
      MYSQL_ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD: "yes"
    command:
      - "--max_connections=1000"
      - "--default-authentication-plugin=mysql_native_password"
      - "--bind-address=127.0.0.1"
    volumes:
      - mysql-data:/var/lib/mysql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "mysqladmin", "ping", "-h", "127.0.0.1", "-uroot"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

      - "-mysql-no-pass"
      - "-listen-addr=127.0.0.1"
      - "-listen-port=3900"
      - "-mysql-dbname=planetscale"
      - "-mysql-addr=127.0.0.1"
      - "-mysql-port=3306"
    depends_on:

        condition: service_healthy

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["redis-server", "--bind", "127.0.0.1", "--port", "6379"]

      timeout: 3s

  serverless-redis-http:
    image: hiett/serverless-redis-http:latest

      SRH_CONNECTION_STRING: "redis://127.0.0.1:6379"
      SRH_PORT: "8079"
    depends_on:
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

  mailhog:
    image: mailhog/mailhog:latest
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    # MailHog binds to all interfaces by default; SMTP on 1025, UI on 8025.

  # One-shot job: install workspace dependencies and push the Prisma schema to

        # boot and render the login page even if the DB isn't ready yet.
        pnpm --filter=@dub/prisma push --accept-data-loss --skip-generate || true
        echo "web-bootstrap: done"

  web:
    image: node:22-bookworm
    network_mode: host
    working_dir: /workspace/apps/web
    restart: unless-stopped

Perfect. Now I have all the information I need. Let me compile my findings:

## Findings Report

**1. No guards preventing middleware re-runs on `/app.dub.co/*` paths**

The codebase lacks any check to prevent middleware from re-executing on rewritten paths. The middleware matcher is global: `"/((?!api/|_next/|_proxy/|favicon.ico|sitemap.xml|robots.txt|manifest.webmanifest).*)"` (/workspace/apps/web/middleware.ts:31), and there's no early exit for paths already rewritten to `/app.dub.co`.

**2. No path prefix stripping logic in parse.ts or app.ts**

The `/workspace/apps/web/lib/middleware/utils/parse.ts` file extracts domain and path but doesn't strip `/app.dub.co/` prefixes. The middleware checks domain against `APP_HOSTNAMES` (/workspace/packages/utils/src/constants/main.ts:6-11), which includes `localhost:8888` and `app.dub.co`. When AppMiddleware rewrites to `/app.dub.co${fullPath}` (/workspace/apps/web/lib/middleware/app.ts:118), the path component stays the same—the rewrite is purely a URL change, not a path transformation.

**3. Local dev convention is `localhost:8888` bare, not subdomains**

Per `/workspace/apps/web/.env.example:11`: `NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:8888`. The constants (/workspace/packages/utils/src/constants/main.ts:9) treat both `localhost:8888` and `localhost` as APP_HOSTNAMES. The parse.ts file (line 11) maps `dub.localhost:8888` to SHORT_DOMAIN. **Production uses subdomain routing (`app.dub.co`), but local dev uses bare `localhost:8888`—the middleware doesn't guard against re-execution because production would never hit the second invocation (different host header).**

**4. Playwright tests use subdomains**

`/workspace/apps/web/playwright.config.ts:20` defaults to `http://partners.localhost:8888`, and workspace tests use `http://app.localhost:8888` (line 45, 52, 66). **This is a mismatch with the default dev env—tests run against subdomains, but `.env.example` assumes bare `localhost:8888`.**

**5. `runtime: "nodejs"` is the only middleware config**

`runtime: "nodejs"` appears only in `/workspace/apps/web/middleware.ts:22`. This is Next.js 15's experimental Node.js middleware runtime (as opposed to Edge). **Unlike Edge runtime, Node.js runtime doesn't skip re-execution on internal rewrites—it processes each matched request through the full middleware pipeline, explaining the double invocation.**

**Root cause:** With `runtime: "nodejs"` and bare `localhost:8888` (single hostname), the rewrite to `/app.dub.co` doesn't change the Host header, so the matcher re-triggers on the rewritten path. Edge runtime would bypass this, but Node.js doesn't. The production app avoids this because `app.dub.co` is a different domain entirely, hitting different middleware logic.

content.text: The dev server's `runtime: "nodejs"` causes middleware to re-run on rewrites (Edge runtime would not). The cleanest fix is to exclude the route-group prefix paths from the matcher so the rewrite target doesn't re-trigger middleware:

input.new_string:
runtime: "nodejs",
  matcher: [
    /*
     * Match all paths except for:
     * 1. /api/ routes
     * 2. /_next/ (Next.js internals)
     * 3. /_proxy/ (proxies for third-party services)
     * 4. The app/api/admin/partners route-group prefixes — middleware
     *    rewrites the public path to one of these (e.g. /login ->
     *    /app.dub.co/login). With `runtime: "nodejs"` middleware re-runs on
     *    internal rewrites (unlike the Edge runtime), so excluding these
     *    prefixes prevents an immediate redirect loop on the rewritten path.
     * 5. Metadata files: favicon.ico, sitemap.xml, robots.txt, manifest.webmanifest
     */
    "/((?!api/|_next/|_proxy/|app\\.dub\\.co/|api\\.dub\\.co/|admin\\.dub\\.co/|partners\\.dub\\.co/|favicon.ico|sitemap.xml|robots.txt|manifest.webmanifest).*)",
  ],
};

content.text:
Workspace is set up and pushed ✨🚀

**What's running at http://localhost:8080:** Dub's full Next.js dashboard. The `/login` page renders with email + Google/GitHub/SAML SSO buttons, the Framer customer card on the right, footer with terms/privacy — Playwright snapshot and screenshot both clean, no console errors.

**What was checked in:**
- `docker-compose.alloy.yaml` — MySQL + ps-http-sim PlanetScale proxy, Redis + hiett/serverless-redis-http (Upstash REST emulator), MailHog, Caddy, web bootstrap (pnpm install + `build:packages` + prisma db push), and the Next.js dev server. All services run with `network_mode: host`.
- `.alloy/environment.json` — `dockerComposePath: docker-compose.alloy.yaml`, `homeUrl: /login`.
- `.alloy/web.env` — placeholder values for the env vars whose module-level constructors (Stripe, Tinybird, NextAuth) would otherwise refuse to load.
- `.alloy/Caddyfile` — reverse proxy `:8080 → 127.0.0.1:8888`. Rewrites `Host` to `localhost:8888` on the way in (Dub hardcodes that string in `APP_HOSTNAMES`) and rewrites the `Location` header back to `localhost:8080` on the way out so dashboard redirects don't leak the upstream port.
- One-line edit to `apps/web/middleware.ts` — added `/app.dub.co/`, `/api.dub.co/`, `/admin.dub.co/`, `/partners.dub.co/` to the matcher exclusion. With `runtime: "nodejs"` middleware re-fires on internal rewrites (Edge runtime would skip), so without this exclusion `/login` immediately bounces to `/login?next=/app.dub.co/login` in a loop.

Pushed to `slavko-bojanic/alloy-setup-our-workspace-please-PRzmV5`.
